justification: Consolidation P2 part 1: a new backend Housing-SEPP eligibility engine (the single source of truth) plus a TOD-catchment fetcher. Substantial new planning-eligibility logic, but it is NOT yet wired into any live path (the brief and the LEP/SEPP tab consume it in follow-up PRs), so there is no current user-facing impact; reviewed at standard tier with full unit coverage.

pre_impl.existing_data: housing_sepp_standards (development_type, standard_type, numeric_value, applicable_zones, requires_lmr_area) holds the LMR/Housing-SEPP forms + thresholds. portal_constraints already had _query_eplanning_point + fetch_sepp_exclusions (776) + fetch_dual_occ_prohibition (452); this adds fetch_tod_catchment (752/759 published TOD polygons).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The only prior implementation is the frontend route.ts, which trusted caller-supplied inLMRArea (defaulted true — silently over-eligible) and a mock Haversine station list. The backend engine computes both authoritatively (776 exclusion -> inLMRArea, conservatively false when unknown; 752/759 polygons -> TOD), so it cannot over-state eligibility on a transient gate failure.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New file services/housing_sepp_eligibility.py ports the route.ts gate logic to the backend (prior-art-checked acknowledged in the module header). Reuses the standards table + the existing ePlanning point-query fetchers; adds only the 752/759 TOD layers + fetch_tod_catchment. db_config.get_connection() is broken in this environment (Supabase pooler SNI), so the engine uses the same direct psycopg2(DATABASE_URL) pattern as the brief's _get_db_conn.

functions.name: evaluate_eligibility
functions.input: zone code, lot area (m2), lot width (m), lat, lng, and optional pre-fetched gate_inputs
functions.output: a list of FormEligibility per development type, each with an eligible flag and a plain-language reason
functions.if_none: a non-residential zone or an unavailable standards table returns an empty list so the caller keeps base controls

functions.name: _gate_inputs
functions.input: the subject lot latitude and longitude (either may be None)
functions.output: a dict of the three authoritative gate booleans in_lmr_area, in_tod and dual_occ_prohibited
functions.if_none: missing coordinates or any failed ArcGIS query yields all-False so no form is ever falsely made eligible

functions.name: fetch_tod_catchment
functions.input: the subject lot latitude and longitude as floats
functions.output: a dict with in_tod plus the source EPI and LGA names, or None when both layer queries error
functions.if_none: when both 752 and 759 queries fail it returns None so the caller treats the catchment as unknown

values: N/A - no regulatory values are hardcoded. All thresholds (min lot size/width, applicable zones, requires_lmr_area) are read live from housing_sepp_standards; the catchment and exclusion answers come live from the published ePlanning layers.

queries.purpose: fetch all Housing-SEPP standards (forms, thresholds, applicable zones, LMR flag) for grouping in Python
queries.where_clause: none required — the whole small curated reference table is read and grouped in memory, not filtered per property
queries.if_0_rows: evaluate_eligibility returns an empty list so the caller keeps the base planning controls (fail-safe)
queries.if_wrong_rows: N/A — it reads the entire reference table, so there is no per-property WHERE that could select wrong rows

break_it.scenario: A lot that is genuinely not in a Low and Mid-Rise area but the caller (old frontend) assumed it was
break_it.what_happens: The frontend default-true made LMR forms falsely eligible there
break_it.how: _gate_inputs derives in_lmr_area from the live 776 exclusion and defaults it False when unknown; requires_lmr_area forms are then ineligible

break_it.scenario: An R3 lot with residential flats that is outside any Transport Oriented Development catchment
break_it.what_happens: A mock-station Haversine check could wrongly qualify it for a mid-rise flat building
break_it.how: residential_flat_r3r4 forms require in_tod from the published 752/759 polygons; outside the catchment they are marked ineligible

break_it.scenario: Any of the live gate queries (776, 452, 752, 759) times out or errors during evaluation
break_it.what_happens: A naive engine could crash the brief or over-restrict/over-permit the affected forms
break_it.how: every gate query is wrapped in try/except returning the conservative False, and a missing standards table returns an empty list

break_it.scenario: A lot whose width or area is unknown because lot geometry could not be resolved upstream
break_it.what_happens: Comparing an unknown dimension to a minimum could pass by accident or raise
break_it.how: an unconfirmed (None) area or width against a real minimum is treated as ineligible with an 'unconfirmed' reason, never as a pass

break_it.scenario: The housing_sepp_standards reference query fails because the database is unreachable or the statement times out
break_it.what_happens: An unhandled error in _fetch_standards_grouped would raise and break whatever consumes the engine
break_it.how: evaluate_eligibility wraps the _fetch_standards_grouped call in try/except and returns an empty list, so the caller keeps the base planning controls

post_merge.manual_verify: This module is not yet wired. Next PR (P2 part 2) derives the capacity brief ceiling from the densest ELIGIBLE form here (subsuming P1's _eligibility_excluded_forms); P3 migrates the LEP/SEPP tab to call it via a backend endpoint so the two surfaces stop disagreeing. Verified live the gates resolve correctly (Ashfield in-TOD -> R3 flats eligible; Five Dock not-TOD -> R3 flats absent).
